page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-88 is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 88 dedicated vCPUs across 44 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz with two threads per core. The instance configuration includes 352 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 105 MB of L3 cache along with advanced instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8). It does not include dedicated hardware accelerators or bundled local storage, requiring persistent storage to be attached over the network.

Benchmark metrics show strong multi-core computational power and high memory subsystem bandwidth. The instance achieved top-quartile performance in multi-core stress-ng tests (73300.5), Geekbench multi-core execution (18648.0), and Clang software compilation (50671.0). Large-block uncached memory read throughput reached 225.15 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reached 79.08 GB/sec. Extended instruction evaluations and image processing tests placed in upper performance tiers, aided by hardware matrix acceleration. In contrast, single-core benchmark results, including single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores, aligned with mid-tier averages, indicating that total processing capacity relies heavily on thread parallelization.

From a cost and resource allocation perspective, c3-standard-88 offers high compute density and large memory capacity within a non-accelerated tier. Because local NVMe storage is omitted, workloads sensitive to low disk latency depend entirely on external storage volumes. The server is well suited for horizontally and vertically scaled multi-threaded applications, including Redis in-memory caching, high-volume database operations, large-scale CI/CD build farms, static web hosting, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-88 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 88 dedicated vCPUs (44 physical cores) on a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor and 352 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with 105 MB of L3 cache, it supports AVX-512 and AMX instructions for vector and matrix computation. The instance omits local disk storage and discrete GPUs, relying on external network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded performance, yielding high marks in multi-core compilation, PassMark CPU tests, and static web serving throughput exceeding 79 GB/sec, alongside an uncached memory read bandwidth of 225.15 GB/sec. Single-core performance remains average. With its balanced 1:4 allocation ratio, this configuration provides cost-efficient processing capacity for enterprise web serving, large-scale Redis caching, build environments, and multi-threaded data transformation pipelines.
